analysis.title: US Capital Markets Perspectives, October 2026
key_insights: Federated Hermes projects global GDP growth of 3% for 2026. US Q2 2026 GDP grew 2.2% annualized, led by AI-related business investment, manufacturing and consumer spending.
Inflation remains sticky and above the Fed's 2% target. High energy, freight and food costs are sustaining it and weighing on consumers.
The Fed raised rates by 0.25% on September 16, 2026. FOMC members and markets anticipate further hikes. Inflation has overtaken the labor market as the immediate policy concern.
The September US jobs report was weaker than expected, but unemployment is low at 4.2%.
AI has fueled equity gains mainly through capex. Hyperscalers are issuing record debt in 2026, which competes with the Treasury market for buyers.
Yields have risen on inflation fears, Fed policy and geopolitical concerns. The 10-year Treasury yield is up 132 basis points since the start of the Iran war, reaching 5.29% as of 9/30/26.
The 10-year term premium has also risen. Real yields are rising because of resilient growth, heavy AI capex and large government debt supply.
Oil rose above $100 per barrel after the Iran war began and has fluctuated around that level since. Disinflation has stalled on energy supply shocks and geopolitical conflict.
The ECB, Bank of Japan and Fed have begun raising rates, while the Bank of England has held.
In Q1 2026, AI-related investment contributed 1.34 percentage points to the US economy's 2% growth. The AI boom is in year three, when prior booms peaked.
Federated Hermes forecasts 2026E/2027E: real GDP 2.3%/2.9%, core CPI 2.8%/2.4%, core PCE 3.2%/2.6%, 10-year yield 5.00%/4.75%, upper Fed funds limit 4.25%/4.50%.
Federated Hermes targets S&P 500 EPS of $370 (2026E) and $425 (2027E), at a 20.0x/20.4x forward P/E, for an index target of 8,500 and 10,000.

Disinflation requires lower energy prices. Policy error becomes a risk if the Fed hikes more than markets expect while growth weakens under higher mortgage and variable-rate costs and falling sentiment.

Diversification is recommended as market strength broadens beyond top tech into international and emerging markets, US small caps and alternatives. It may also mitigate inflation, volatility and fiscal policy risk from the US mid-term elections.

Scenario-specific allocations: resilient growth favors US equities, international developed large caps, intermediate and corporate bonds. Inflation persistence favors dividend and value stocks and short-term or floating-rate bonds. Productivity-led growth favors growth equities, emerging markets and high yield. A hard landing favors alternatives, money market and government bonds.

sector_views.rationale: Favored in the productivity-led growth scenario, where AI broadens and inflation cools.
Favored in the inflation persistence scenario, where growth weakens and inflation stays sticky.

risk_factors: Policy error if the Fed hikes more than markets expect while growth weakens amid higher mortgage and variable-rate costs and falling sentiment.
Energy prices must fall for disinflation to start. Oil above $100 keeps inflation sticky.
Downside shock or hard landing is a tail risk. Signs of softening growth and rate-dampened housing could increasingly affect investment and spending.
Record hyperscaler debt issuance competes with the Treasury market, and heavy government debt supply is pushing real yields higher.
Mid-term election outcomes may bring fiscal policy changes and volatility.
charts_described: US Treasury yield curve chart compares 2/27/26 and 9/30/26. The 10-year yield is 5.29% on 9/30/26 and the 30-year is 5.68%.
Global GDP growth chart shows 2026 consensus estimates by region, including the US at 2.3% and China at 4.6%.
vol_and_positioning: Volatility has been a constant in bond markets, with Treasury yields moving on shifting Fed expectations and inflation concerns.
Markets have already priced in much of the further Fed tightening that recent inflation prints may support.
geopolitical: The Iran war began earlier in 2026. Oil rose above $100 per barrel and has fluctuated around it, and the 10-year yield is up 132 basis points since.
Geopolitical conflicts and energy supply shocks have stalled the global disinflation trend.
US mid-term elections may bring more pronounced trends and potential fiscal policy changes.

tension_points.bull_case: Resilient growth, AI-led productivity and strong household and hyperscaler balance sheets could let core inflation fall and the Fed ease without a recession.
tension_points.bear_case: Hiking more than markets expect while growth weakens under surging mortgage and variable-rate costs and falling sentiment would be a policy error.
tension_points.what_invalidates: Energy prices staying high would keep disinflation from starting, and weakening growth alongside further hikes would undercut the bull case.
